title: Review verdict (.github)
description:
The bundle's shape, narrowed to the one reviewing role this repository runs and to the pull-request scope vocabulary of ADR-085 §E.16. The three-state `decision`, the `findings` shape and the `checks_run` contract are the base's; the vocabulary here is local, and `tag` is added on a finding. §E.16's classes carry spaces, which the base permits: it bounds `scope_class` by length and nothing else, so a class reaches the verdict spelled the way the pull-request body spells it.

`agent` is the role, not the routine: `docs-guardrails-review.md` is a document a runner is handed, and the same role would still be the author if that file were split or renamed. The five `unevaluatedProperties: false` — the root, a finding, a check entry, a handoff, a `parts` entry — are this file's because the base declares none; the base's own `description` says why the closers belong here, and `agents_file_check.py` names any object that ends up without one.

part.description: The part of `docs-guardrails-review.md` a verdict judged, where the routine runs as parts, one run each. Absent on a verdict of the whole routine. `repo` is the calling repository's own extension; the other four are the routine's `## Part` sections. The same role is the author whatever part it judged, which is why this is a field and not a value of `agent`.

parts.description: What each part of a review that ran as parts came to, on the verdict aggregated from them. `reviewed` carries the part's own decision; `skipped` means the part applied to no file of the pull request and says why; `missing` means the part was to run and produced no verdict that satisfies this schema, and says why. A `missing` part makes the aggregate incomplete: the findings of the parts that did report stand, and the required check does not pass on them.

tag.description: The bracketed severity this finding carries, and optional because a finding need not be tagged. It belongs to the finding rather than to the verdict: one review reports a `[HARD BLOCK]` and a `[DOC DEBT]` in the same run, and ADR-087 §B.7 maps a finding's tag to a label. The enum is the seven severities `docs-guardrails-review.md` emits and no others: a value nobody can check against a file in this repository is a value the routine may never emit. The rest of the review vocabulary — `CATEGORY-C`, `SYNC`, `PERFORMANCE`, `PHASE`, `HEURISTIC` — lives in `pr-review.md`, the Claude Project document ADR-085 §J.33 still points at, and is left out on purpose until that document is in git and can be checked the same way.

part.description: The part whose run raised this finding, on a verdict aggregated from parts.
